content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":6,"description_fidelity":7,"readability_1x":7,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":8,"appeal":7},"score":66,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The cyan domed body and dangling legs read as a small floating squid, but the eyes are not clearly identifiable at 1x.","The lower-center face and tentacle area contains cramped black-and-blue clusters that merge into visual noise.","The large white patch on the body's left side reads more like a missing chunk than controlled metallic highlighting.","The tentacles have similar lengths and heavy black gaps, making the gathered-versus-thrust motion difficult to infer.","Nothing in the normal pose strongly communicates the mine function or provides an obvious pair of pixels that could flash red.","The body is cleanly outlined, but the lower silhouette lacks the economical, strongly patterned construction typical of MM2/MM3 enemies."],"fixes":["Replace the lower-center blue maze with two clearly separated eye pixels or eye blocks, leaving black spacing around each.","Reserve those eye pixels for a red warning frame so the flashing state is immediately legible.","Reduce the white body highlight to a compact 2x2 or stepped cluster and restore cyan around it.","Simplify the underside into three distinct tentacle groups with clean one-pixel gaps and fewer internal black notches.","Create at least two animation poses: tentacles tucked inward beneath the body, then extended downward and outward for thrust.","Regularize the lower outline into deliberate one-pixel stair-steps and remove isolated blue pixels trapped inside the black structure."]}
